papers.title: Systematic Evaluation of Adversarial Jailbreaking Attacks and Defenses Across Seven Large Language Models
papers.summary: Large language models (LLMs) deployed in safety-critical settings must resist adversarial inputs designed to elicit harmful outputs. We present a systematic empirical evaluation of five adversarial jailbreaking attack families---direct requests, roleplay-based jailbreaking, hypothetical framing, instruction override, and obfuscation---across seven open-weight and API-accessible LLMs: Llama-3-8B, Llama-3.1-8B, Llama-3.2-3B, Mistral-7B, Qwen2.5-7B, Gemma2-9B, and Phi-4-14B. We further evaluate four defense mechanisms: keyword blacklisting, self-reminder prompting, paraphrase-based sanitization, and perplexity-based filtering against the two most vulnerable models. Our results reveal that obfuscation attacks achieve a mean attack success rate (ASR) of 54.3% across all models and constitute the most transferable adversarial vector, bypassing every evaluated model with nonzero success. We find that model size does not predict adversarial robustness (Spearman r=-0.57, p=0.18), and that models within the same architecture family exhibit dramatically different vulnerability profiles. Self-reminder prompting achieves the most consistent defense, reducing ASR from 44% to 10% on Mistral-7B and from 48% to 5% on Llama-3.1-8B with zero false positives and no additional inference cost. Our code and datasets are publicly available at https://github.com/Mdniloykhan/jailbreak-eval-7llms.
papers.title_zh: 七个大型语言模型上对抗性越狱攻击与防御的系统性评估
papers.abstract_zh: 部署在安全关键环境中的大型语言模型（LLM）必须抵御旨在诱导有害输出的对抗性输入。我们对五类对抗性越狱攻击——直接请求、基于角色扮演的越狱、假设性框架、指令覆盖和混淆——在七个开放权重和可通过 API 访问的 LLM 上进行了系统性的实证评估：Llama-3-8B、Llama-3.1-8B、Llama-3.2-3B、Mistral-7B、Qwen2.5-7B、Gemma2-9B 和 Phi-4-14B。我们进一步针对两个最脆弱的模型评估了四种防御机制：关键词黑名单、自我提醒提示、基于改写的净化以及基于困惑度的过滤。我们的结果表明，混淆攻击在所有模型上达到 54.3% 的平均攻击成功率（ASR），并构成最具可迁移性的对抗性向量，以非零成功率绕过了每一个被评估的模型。我们发现模型规模并不能预测对抗鲁棒性（Spearman r=-0.57，p=0.18），并且同一架构家族内的模型表现出显著不同的脆弱性特征。自我提醒提示实现了最一致的防御，在 Mistral-7B 上将 ASR 从 44% 降至 10%，在 Llama-3.1-8B 上从 48% 降至 5%，且零假阳性、无额外推理成本。我们的代码和数据集公开可用，地址为 https://github.com/Mdniloykhan/jailbreak-eval-7llms。

papers.title: Judging Before Propagation: Task-Graph Contextual Integrity for Multi-Agent Privacy
papers.summary: Multi-agent LLM systems increasingly rely on persistent memory and inter-agent communication. These capabilities create privacy risks that extend beyond individual interactions: a release appropriate in isolation may become inappropriate when combined with information previously disclosed to a recipient or propagated to downstream agents along the planned workflow. Existing Contextual Integrity (CI) mechanisms for agentic systems typically rely on local judgments that assess each disclosure in isolation, with or without regard to the recipient's history, but do not account for how information propagates downstream. However, compliance at the current boundary does not guarantee appropriateness across the workflow. We introduce Task-Graph Contextual Integrity (TG-CI), to our knowledge the first task-graph-native formalization of Contextual Integrity for multi-agent systems. TG-CI represents a workflow as a Multi-Agent Task Graph (MATG) and extends CI from atomic transfers to stateful, graph-level information flows by jointly considering an item's intended propagation scope and recipients' evolving disclosure states. We operationalize TG-CI through propagation-scoped authorization under two complementary policies: Full-Scope, which requires admissibility across the complete downstream scope, and Auto-Region, which confines each item to its maximal admissible region using lightweight frontier gates. We further introduce MAPLE-Bench, a benchmark of 144 cases across four scenarios that jointly vary MATG topology, disclosure history, compromised-agent placement, and item-level privacy policies. In our primary experimental configuration, TG-CI reduces the mean unauthorized disclosure count by 85.8-94.1% relative to the Local-History CI baseline, while retaining 93.6-96.1% of the baseline's task accuracy, with the two enforcement policies providing complementary privacy--cost--utility trade-offs.

papers.title: RV2GC: Reconstructing the Garbling Boundary in a RISC-V Garbled Processor
papers.summary: Programmable garbled-circuit execution must balance the benefits of cross-program reuse against the cost of repeated work during secure execution. A complete garbled processor provides a fixed circuit for many programs, but its evaluator repeatedly visits processor-wide structures even when only a small part performs the current protected computation. We present RV2GC, which reconstructs the garbling boundary around a fixed library of RISC-V instruction circuits. Public scheduling and operand routing operate outside the circuit topologies; persistent label-encoded state connects independently invoked garbled instruction circuits and instruction-specific garbling-free paths through a common interface. A Conditional-execution Stack and protected commits support secret-dependent branches, bounded loops, and secret-indexed memory access under public scheduling, keeping instruction and memory-address sequences independent of private inputs. Across nine benchmarks, measured ARM2GC-to-RV2GC runtime ratios range from 12.81 to 4,043. In terms of circuit size, the largest listed instruction circuit has 3,386 gates, corresponding to 2.044% and 0.393% of the 256-byte and 4,096-byte Amber processors, respectively. Additional comparisons quantify schedule storage, communication, and the cost of secret-dependent execution.

papers.title: Cybersecurity Practices in Industrial Automation and Control Systems: a Study of Croatian System Integrators
papers.summary: Given the increasing frequency of industrial cybersecurity incidents, governments, industry, and the research community are all working to find ways to protect industrial automation and control systems (IACSs). A key regulatory effort in the European context is the EU's Network and Information Security Directive 2 (NIS2), which aims to strengthen cybersecurity requirements and improve resilience across critical and important sectors. Nevertheless, translating cybersecurity requirements into practical engineering remains challenging within IACS environments. This paper explores how Croatian IACS system integrators perceive cybersecurity requirements, implementation challenges, and current practices in the industrial environments in which they operate. The findings are based on three focus groups with system integrators working with clients in the energy, chemical and pharmaceutical, and food and beverage sectors. Participants reported limited cybersecurity awareness among IACS owners, as well as perceived differences in practices between smaller and larger companies and between domestic and foreign firms. Participants were divided in their expectations regarding regulatory pressure: while some believed it could improve cybersecurity, others expected only minimal compliance focused on cost reduction. The results of this study provide a basis for developing more practical cybersecurity practices and offer a deeper understanding of the key challenges faced by IACS system integrators and owners when dealing with cybersecurity.

papers.title: PairWatch: Pair-Aware Anomaly Transformer for Detecting Adversarial Rendezvous in Public Satellite Catalogs
papers.summary: Documented adversarial rendezvous and proximity operations (RPO) appear in the public TLE catalog, yet existing TLE-based maneuver detectors treat each satellite in isolation - mistaking routine station-keeping for adversarial behavior and missing RPO entirely when the target stays passive. We argue that the right unit is the satellite pair and the right inductive bias is the kinematic symmetry between approach and recede. We instantiate both with PairWatch, a pair-aware AnomalyTransformer whose attention prior is augmented with a sign-symmetric geometric similarity over relative-motion features, and release an open benchmark of 359 windows from public Space-Track data spanning 11 documented RPO events, 100 Clohessy-Wiltshire synthetic adversarial windows, and a five-class hard-negative set culminating in the TerraSAR-X / TanDEM-X helix formation. Under the deployment-relevant criterion of a single threshold separating real RPO from operational negatives - a necessary property for catalog-scale screening - PairWatch is the only model that succeeds, with the property holding in 100% of bootstrap resamples versus 0-19.5% for three neural baselines and under 0.1% for four physics-informed detectors. A per-source analysis exposes a shortcut-learning failure mode of single-number AUROC: simpler baselines attain higher overall AUROC by shortcutting a synthetic-vs-formation contrast with no operational meaning; removing this single cell flips the test ranking entirely (LSTM-AD), and these baselines fail the security-relevant task the benchmark was built to measure.

papers.title: Hardware-Aware Model Inversion in Memristive Spiking Neural Networks
papers.summary: Hardware-accelerated spiking neural networks (SNNs) implemented on memristive crossbar arrays offer significant gains in energy efficiency, while device variability and analog noise are sometimes assumed to hinder information extraction. However, whether these hardware effects improve, preserve, or degrade privacy after deployment remains largely unexplored. Therefore, we ask whether model-inversion leakage characterized on an SNN remains representative after the same model is mapped to a non-ideal memristive substrate, and how hardware non-idealities and reliability faults affecting synapses, neuron thresholds, and spike processing reshape that leakage. To study this problem, we introduce Spiking Domain Model Inversion (SDMI), an inversion method that combines Expectation over Transformation (EOT) with surrogate gradients to optimize inputs through stochastic analog behavior and non-differentiable spiking dynamics. We use SDMI consistently across the SNN model, its memristive SNN, and the same memristive SNN under additional hardware perturbations. Across four datasets, reconstruction leakage does not vary monotonically with model accuracy or hardware variability. At comparable accuracy levels, neuron-threshold perturbations increase reconstruction fidelity, measured by SSIM, by up to 51.8%, whereas spike-level perturbations primarily degrade utility without consistently improving reconstruction. Weight noise, in contrast, reduces leakage under the same inversion procedure. These results show that hardware variability is not inherently privacy-preserving: model inversion leakage in memristive SNNs depends on the hardware state and cannot be inferred from model accuracy alone.

papers.title: Investigating Data Flows from Android Games
papers.summary: Online applications can share data with arbitrary parties, without users noticing. In practice, these data flows could constitute privacy violations to individual users, with the lack of transparency leaving users unaware of the unwanted data flows. To understand the spread and scale of this privacy threat, we investigate what data is collected and where it is sent in popular free-to-play Android games. As part of our investigation, we conduct a measurement study where we collect and analyze over 16 GB of network traffic from 50 puzzle games. Additionally, we explore the effectiveness of user-side countermeasures for a selection of the apps. We find that while most countermeasures, such as ad-blocking DNS services, decrease data flows, withholding consent and opting out of data collection can produce inconsistent behavior including increased outgoing traffic. To encourage further analysis, we release our measurements as an open dataset.

papers.title: SEAL: Sealed Queries for Local Sanitization against Indirect Prompt Injection
papers.summary: Indirect prompt injection threatens local LLM agents through untrusted tool outputs, motivating defenses that suppress attacks while preserving task evidence under limited inference budgets. We introduce SEAL, which learns a soft prompt and scoring readout offline to sanitize tool outputs using a frozen task model. SEAL constructs scoring queries from trusted initial context and the learned prompt, keeping the reference independent of inspected tool text. It scores tokens without normalization across context tokens and uses preservation regularization to encourage retention of useful evidence during localized deletion. This design requires neither defense-generated tokens nor a separate verifier model. Across AgentDojo and AgentDyn, SEAL suppresses attacks while improving task completion under attack. Specifically, on AgentDojo, SEAL reduces attack success from 34.6\% to 0.1\% and increases Joint---task completion without attack success---from 51.4\% to 77.5\%, while using approximately $127\times$ fewer defense-related tokens than PISanitizer, a state-of-the-art prompt injection defense. Replication on a second backbone with the same training recipe supports applicability across model families.

papers.title: InferD: A Honeypot Framework for AI Inference Infrastructure
papers.summary: Large language model serving stacks, commercial inference APIs, vector databases, and agent orchestration gateways are now ex- posed on the public internet and indexed by commodity scanners within hours of deployment. The threat characteristics of this sur- face are only beginning to be measured, and the honeypot frame- works that could measure it were designed for conventional net- work services rather than for AI infrastructure. In fact, emulating an AI service is a distinct deception problem: the observable behavior of the service, including model inventories, token formats, tool-call protocols, and authorization flows, must be reproduced faithfully, while the underlying computation, model inference and tool ex- ecution, must never occur. We present InferD, a low-interaction honeypot framework organized around a single principle we call deception without inference: every request an adversary can observe is answered from static response pools, and nothing an adversary submits is ever executed. InferD decomposes the emulation into four deception planes, transport, service protocol, vulnerability surface, and agentic session, adds a provenance plane that links a planted credential to evidence of downstream model-mediated processing.
papers.title_zh: InferD：面向 AI 推理基础设施的蜜罐框架
papers.abstract_zh: 大型语言模型服务栈、商业推理 API、向量数据库和智能体编排网关如今已暴露在公共互联网上，并在部署后数小时内被现成扫描器索引。这一攻击面的威胁特征才刚刚开始被测量，而能够测量它的蜜罐框架是为传统网络服务而非 AI 基础设施设计的。事实上，模拟 AI 服务是一个独特的欺骗问题：包括模型清单、令牌格式、工具调用协议和授权流程在内的可观察行为必须被忠实复现，而底层计算、模型推理和工具执行绝不能发生。我们提出 InferD，一个低交互蜜罐框架，围绕我们称为“无推理的欺骗”的单一原则组织：对手能够观察到的每个请求都由静态响应池作答，且对手提交的任何内容都不会被执行。InferD 将模拟分解为四个欺骗平面：传输、服务协议、漏洞面和智能体会话，并增加一个溯源平面，将植入的凭证与下游模型介导处理的证据关联起来。

papers.title: Integrating Perception, Comprehension, and Projection for Alert Validation: A Unified Cyber Situational Awareness Framework
papers.summary: Security Operation Centres (SOCs) must validate large volumes of alerts with limited analyst resources, yet alerts often lack sufficient context to determine whether suspicious activity is attack related. While provenance-based intrusion detection research has progressed from perception-level signals to comprehension- and projection-level cyber situational awareness (CSA), it remains unclear whether richer CSA consistently improves alert validation. This paper presents the first systematic evaluation of perception-, comprehension-,and projection-level CSA within a unified alert validation framework. Using Captain and Kairos, we generate multi-level CSA and formulate alert validation as a positive-unlabelled multi-instance learning (PU-MIL) task over CSA-derived behavioural hypotheses. Experimental evaluation on the DARPA TC dataset shows that comprehension-level CSA substantially improves validation by incorporating causal attack context. Relative to the Queue and Max. CSG baselines, PU-MIL achieves up to 28.6 and 75 percentage-point gains in Recall@5, and 24.6% and 86.8% reductions in mean positive rank on Cadets and Theia, respectively. Projection-level CSA can yield additional benefits, reducing the mean positive rank on Theia from 22.0 to 8.5 at a 40-minute projection horizon, although its effectiveness varies across projection horizons. Overall, richer CSA does not necessarily lead to better alert validation. Rather, its value depends on when and how it is introduced, motivating adaptive CSA progression that selectively enriches alerts according to validation requirements.

papers.title: Syndrome Trellis Decryption in Post-Quantum Cryptography
papers.summary: We present a novel post-quantum cryptographic framework based on masked high-memory convolutional codes in the Niederreiter paradigm. The public key is derived from a high-memory polynomial parity-check matrix augmented by dense random masking and additional invertible linear transformations. The resulting matrix exhibits strong random-like properties, effectively concealing its algebraic structure and resisting known structural and algebraic attacks. Legitimate recipients retain polynomial-time decoding capability, whereas adversaries appear to be limited to generic information-set decoding with exponential complexity. Under standard cryptanalytic estimates, the proposed construction achieves security margins exceeding those of classical McEliece- and Niederreiter-based systems by factors greater than 2^200. Beyond its enhanced security profile, the construction offers considerable design flexibility, supporting arbitrary plaintext lengths, linear-time decryption, and a uniform per-bit computational cost, enabling efficient scalability to very long messages. Practical implementation is facilitated by a parallel array of syndrome-trellis decoders, dynamically instantiated according to candidate syndrome values, enabling efficient hardware and software implementations with high throughput. Overall, the proposed scheme is a promising candidate for robust, scalable, quantum-resistant public-key cryptography.

papers.title: From if to Oops: Turning a conditional into a key-recovery oracle
papers.summary: Deterministic variants of CSIDH remove randomness from the group action, either through implementation techniques or, as in Houben's deterministic CSIDH and OSIDH-LD, by design. Since earlier fault attacks on CSIDH mostly target random point sampling, determinism seems to close that avenue. We show that it opens another: every secret-dependent step occurs at a fixed, public point of every execution, so an attacker can fault the same step repeatedly. Our attack forces the mask that selects which of two lanes computes the next isogeny to zero, for example by skipping one instruction. Whether the output changes reveals whether a secret exponent reaches a chosen threshold, and a binary search over these thresholds recovers the full key with one fault per execution: at most 297 oracle queries for OSIDH-LD and 222 for deterministic CSIDH with CSIDH-512-sized keys. We recover full OSIDH-LD keys in a software fault simulation of the reference implementation, and show on a ChipWhisperer-Lite that the targeted instruction is skipped with probability at least 0.94 at an isolated fault position. Finally, we argue that fault resistance requires giving up determinism, and propose countermeasures relying on randomization.

papers.title: Attack-Resilient Multi-Bit Image Watermarking Framework via Latent Coordinate Sign Clamping
papers.summary: Watermarking is essential for image copyright protection and attribution, yet existing methods suffer from fundamental trade-offs among post-hoc applicability to pre-existing images, multi-bit capacity, training-free deployment, and adversarial resilience. To address these limitations, we propose a training-free watermarking framework that exploits the overcompleteness of diffusion latent spaces to embed multi-bit payloads into arbitrary images while preserving high visual quality. Additionally, we develop a three-layer decoding pipeline that combines magnitude-weighted majority voting, BCH, and Chase decoding to maximize message-extraction accuracy in the presence of channel noise. To counter active adversaries, our framework integrates a steganalysis-resistant noise camouflage layer and a dual-layer forgery defense that combines perceptual hashing with a Reed-Solomon fuzzy commitment scheme over CLIP features. Empirical evaluations demonstrate that our method applies to both natural and AI-generated images with a scalable $32\text{--}128$-bit capacity. Furthermore, it effectively mitigates advanced removal vectors ($94.6\%$ decode rate against CtrlRegen+ regeneration attacks) and secures robust forgery detection ($98.8\%$ accuracy via joint CLIP and RS fuzzy commitment mechanism).
papers.title_zh: 通过潜在坐标符号钳位实现的抗攻击多比特图像水印框架
papers.abstract_zh: 水印对于图像版权保护与归属溯源至关重要，然而现有方法在对已有图像的事后适用性、多比特容量、免训练部署以及对抗鲁棒性之间存在着根本性的权衡。为解决这些局限，我们提出了一种免训练的水印框架，该框架利用扩散潜在空间的过完备性，将多比特载荷嵌入任意图像，同时保持高视觉质量。此外，我们开发了一种三层解码流水线，将幅度加权多数投票、BCH 与 Chase 解码相结合，以在存在信道噪声的情况下最大化消息提取准确率。为对抗主动攻击者，我们的框架集成了一个抗隐写分析的噪声伪装层，以及一种双层伪造防御机制，该机制将感知哈希与基于 CLIP 特征的 Reed-Solomon 模糊承诺方案相结合。实证评估表明，我们的方法适用于自然图像与 AI 生成图像，并具有可扩展的 $32\text{--}128$ 比特容量。此外，它能够有效抵御先进的移除攻击手段（针对 CtrlRegen+ 再生攻击的解码率达到 $94.6\%$），并实现稳健的伪造检测（通过联合 CLIP 与 RS 模糊承诺机制达到 $98.8\%$ 的准确率）。

papers.title: DYNAS: A Dynamic Network Penetration Testing Framework Using Deep Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary: As network scale and uncertainty complicate automated penetration testing, reinforcement learning (RL) environments must support controlled evaluation under defensive and non-stationary conditions. We present DYNAS (Dynamic Network Attack Simulator), which combines parameterized large-scale scenario generation with stateful intrusion detection responses, explicit scan false-positive and false-negative noise, temporary service unavailability, and duration-based action timeouts. We further introduce Pen-DHRL, a recurrent manager--worker policy that selects persistent subgoals using IDS-conditioned global context. We compare Pen-DHRL with GNN, Invariant, and Attention baselines across four scenario variants and multiple training regimes. Under IDS-disabled training followed by IDS-enabled evaluation, Pen-DHRL obtains approximately 64\% and 24\% higher reward per step on Bridge and Dynamic, respectively, and approximately 26\% and 30\% more captured hosts on VarA and VarB than the next-best baseline. With all defensive dynamics active from the beginning of training, Pen-DHRL achieves positive mean episode returns in all four scenarios, whereas the flat baselines produce negative mean returns in all 12 architecture--scenario combinations; staged curriculum training produces positive mean returns across all 16 evaluated combinations.

papers.title: Understanding and Mitigating Role Spoofing in LLMs
papers.summary: Despite growing capabilities, LLMs remain susceptible to prompt injections: malicious inputs that can manipulate or hijack models. In particular, it has recently been observed that LLMs can exhibit role confusion (Ye et al., 2026), where models attribute the source of text based on its style instead of its labeled role. Malicious text in tool outputs (for instance, a malicious webpage accessed by an agent) can leverage role confusion to impersonate the user, an attack we call role spoofing}. In this work, we seek to understand and mitigate role spoofing. We study how models track "who said what" in a conversation, showing that they use cues from both content (e.g., semantics and writing style) and structure (e.g., control tokens and formatting). We show that LLMs are highly susceptible to role spoofing attacks that combine both fake structure and content. Additionally, in a toy setting, we show that adversarial training which teaches the model to ignore content-based injections does mitigate content-based attacks but leaves the model susceptible to structure-based attacks. This can explain why frontier models, with increased resistance to many injection attacks, can still be susceptible to role spoofing. Finally, we propose a new method for detecting role spoofing using linear probes trained to predict roles in a conversation, and show that it is effective across different settings.

papers.title: Deep Learning Based Behavioral Drift Modeling for Continuous Biometric Authentication
papers.summary: This research proposes a two-level keystroke dynamics authentication system that provides defense-in-depth security through continuous behavioral drift monitoring. Level 1 employs fixed-text password authentication using Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCN) with contrastive learning and population-based training (PBT), achieving 3.77% EER for high-security login verification. Upon successful authentication, Level 2 continuously monitors user typing during natural free-text sessions using a 4-Model Deep Learning Ensemble. If suspicious behavioral drift is detected during monitoring, the system re-authenticates the user by returning to Level 1, providing a feedback loop against session hijacking and behavioral anomalies. The system explicitly models long-term behavioral drift through the fixed-text component's PBT mechanism, which adapts to temporal variations in password typing patterns. This research leverages free-text (Buffalo dataset) and fixed-text (GREYC dataset) keystroke dynamics datasets, extracting temporal and spatial features including hold times, up-down latencies, down-down intervals, and trigram patterns. The final system achieves 96%+ accuracy for fixed-text authentication (3.77% EER) and 83.53% True Acceptance Rate (TAR) at 5% False Acceptance Rate (FAR) for free-text continuous authentication (10.05% EER), demonstrating superior performance and strong resistance to impostor attacks through continuous behavioral monitoring.

papers.title: RecHash: Segmented Hash-Entangled Chains for Stateful Sequential Authentication
papers.summary: RecHash is a stateful sequential authentication construction based on paired hash-chain openings and an authenticated record history. It develops the decreasing position relation of the 2019 hash-entangled construction, whose exact integer normalization yields a two-coordinate constant-sum antichain. Direct proportional reuse is constrained by integer capacity and multiplicative contraction. The main construction instead assigns each record to a predetermined chain segment, with complementary positions encoding each digest block. All digests fit every scheduled slot, independently of preceding messages. For an $\ell$-bit digest distributed over $k$ equal-length chain pairs, balanced allocation gives $\lfloor L/(2^{\lceil\ell/k\rceil}+1)\rfloor$ slots. A 256-bit digest, 32 pairs, and length 65535 provide 254 application records followed by a renewal certificate, with 2048 bytes of openings per record for 256-bit chain outputs. We give a complete segmented state transition, a worked trace, exact allocation and resource results, and a renewal-free security-composition theorem conditional on authenticated history and an adaptive one-step guarantee. The analysis relates the construction to constant-sum encodings and standardized hash-based signatures; a concrete post-quantum reduction and security across renewal remain open.

papers.title: The Privacy and Security Risks of Edge LLM Optimization
papers.summary: Edge deployment of Large Language Models requires optimization techniques that reduce memory, computation, and energy costs. However, preserving task performance does not necessarily preserve security. We argue that optimization is an information transformation that can alter representations, decision pathways, and trust boundaries, creating security drift and optimization-induced attack surfaces.
papers.title_zh: 边缘 LLM 优化的隐私与安全风险
papers.abstract_zh: 大语言模型的边缘部署需要能够降低内存、计算和能源成本的优化技术。然而，保持任务性能并不必然意味着保持安全性。我们认为，优化是一种信息变换，它可能改变表示、决策路径和信任边界，从而产生安全性漂移和由优化诱导的攻击面。

papers.title: Power Adjusting Games Under Block-Dependent Pool Payout Schemes
papers.summary: Advanced power adjusting block withholding attacks such as PAW and T-PAW have been analyzed so far under a global-reset version of the proportional scheme (GRP), which is rarely used in practice. In this paper, we analyze T-PAW, which contains FAW and PAW as special cases, under the block-dependent payout schemes deployed in practice: Pay-Per-Last-N-Shares (PPLNS), round-based Proportional (PROP) and exponential-decay (EXP). We derive the revenue ratios analytically, by renewal arguments for PPLNS and through the stationary carry process of an open round for PROP and EXP. We further introduce Power Adjusting Hopping (PAH), where an adversary of any size adjusts its power allocation towards the pool according to the blockwork age of the round without withholding any block, and derive its revenue ratios under PROP and EXP. We show that GRP misestimates the T-PAW gain in a scheme-dependent direction: it overstates the gain under PROP up to an order of magnitude and understates it under EXP for the original slush decay rate. PROP is highly vulnerable to PAH, while EXP faces a trade-off: a slow decay invites PAH and a fast decay invites T-PAW. PPLNS is the least vulnerable scheme: it is immune to PAH and it mitigates, but does not eliminate, T-PAW. All analytical results are verified by Monte Carlo simulations.

papers.title: TextSeal2: Distortion-Free LLM Watermarking with Copula Mixing and Memoryless Races
papers.summary: We present TextSeal2, a distortion-free watermark for large language models that keeps its signal under speculative decoding: tokens that replace rejected drafts remain watermarked with the same keys, and the acceptance rate is unchanged. It also preserves output diversity and adds no measurable inference latency. Its predecessor, TextSeal, restores diversity in the Gumbel-max scheme by routing each token to one of two keys via a coin flip. This is suboptimal because the detector averages the scores from both keys without knowing which key was used. TextSeal2 instead merges two or more keys into a single virtual key and couples it to fresh noise through AutoMark's Gaussian copula. Any number of keys, including publicly shared keys, can be merged this way without diluting detection. Under speculative decoding, TextSeal2 verifies keyed drafts with one more exponential race, run on the leftovers of the draft races. By memorylessness, this race reproduces block verification, so the output follows the target model exactly. We evaluate TextSeal2 on three LLMs. At equal output token diversity, TextSeal2 detects 8 to 22 percentage points more 100-token answers than TextSeal at a false-positive rate of $10^{-3}$, and is comparable to textGrain while requiring no post-logits optimization. Under speculative decoding, it detects 18 and 22 percentage points more 200-token answers than TextSeal and textGrain, respectively, at the same acceptance rate.
papers.title_zh: TextSeal2：基于 Copula 混合与无记忆竞赛的无失真 LLM 水印
papers.abstract_zh: 我们提出 TextSeal2，一种面向大语言模型的无失真水印，它能在推测解码下保持其信号：替换被拒绝草稿的 token 仍使用相同的密钥带有水印，且接受率不变。它还保持了输出多样性，并且没有增加可测量的推理延迟。其前身 TextSeal 通过抛硬币将每个 token 路由到两个密钥之一，从而在 Gumbel-max 方案中恢复多样性。这是次优的，因为检测器在不知道使用了哪个密钥的情况下对两个密钥的分数取平均。TextSeal2 则改为将两个或多个密钥合并为单个虚拟密钥，并通过 AutoMark 的高斯 copula 将其与新鲜噪声耦合。任意数量的密钥，包括公开共享的密钥，都可以通过这种方式合并，而不会稀释检测。在推测解码下，TextSeal2 通过再一次指数竞赛来验证带密钥的草稿，该竞赛在草稿竞赛的剩余部分上运行。由于无记忆性，该竞赛复现了块验证，因此输出完全遵循目标模型。我们在三个 LLM 上评估了 TextSeal2。在相同输出 token 多样性下，在 $10^{-3}$ 的假阳性率下，TextSeal2 比 TextSeal 多检测出 8 到 22 个百分点的 100-token 答案，并且与 textGrain 相当，同时无需任何 logits 后优化。在推测解码下，在相同接受率下，它分别比 TextSeal 和 textGrain 多检测出 18 和 22 个百分点的 200-token 答案。

papers.title: AskStream: When and What to Ask Proactively under Uncertainty in Streaming Video Understanding
papers.summary: Recent advances in multimodal large language models have increased interest in interaction paradigms for video understanding. The evolution from offline to streaming and proactive interaction has gradually shifted models from passive responders toward more proactive agents that can decide when to answer. However, existing proactive paradigms typically assume that the information required to answer a query is complete, leaving models to only wait or answer. In the real world, however, information is often incomplete due to uncertainty from either the video or the user. In proactive paradigms, such uncertainty can cause the model to wait forever or generate highly hallucinatory responses. We therefore argue that proactive interaction should be redefined with a third action: ask, allowing models to actively ask for missing information. To study when and what models should ask before answering, we introduce AskStream, the first multi-turn benchmark spanning video and user uncertainty for streaming video understanding, with four task categories and eight subtasks. It contains 438 videos with 2,714 manually annotated frame-level time windows across three types: wait, ask, and answer. Across both multiple-choice and open-ended settings, even the strongest model attains only 52.18% on our proposed Ask-F1 metric, highlighting substantial limitations in proactive information seeking under uncertainty.
papers.title_zh: AskStream：在流式视频理解的不确定性下，何时以及主动询问什么
papers.abstract_zh: 多模态大语言模型的最新进展提高了人们对视频理解交互范式的兴趣。从离线到流式以及主动交互的演进，已逐渐使模型从被动的响应者转变为能够决定何时回答的更加主动的智能体。然而，现有的主动范式通常假设回答查询所需的信息是完整的，这使得模型只能等待或回答。然而在现实世界中，由于视频或用户带来的不确定性，信息往往是不完整的。在主动范式中，这种不确定性可能导致模型永远等待或生成高度幻觉性的回答。因此，我们认为主动交互应通过第三种动作——询问——重新定义，允许模型主动询问缺失的信息。为了研究模型在回答之前应在何时询问以及询问什么，我们引入 AskStream，这是首个面向流式视频理解、涵盖视频与用户不确定性的多轮基准，包含四个任务类别和八个子任务。它包含 438 个视频，以及跨三种类型——等待、询问和回答——的 2,714 个人工标注的帧级时间窗口。在多项选择和开放式设置中，即使最强的模型在我们提出的 Ask-F1 指标上也仅达到 52.18%，这凸显了在不确定性下主动信息寻求方面存在重大局限。

papers.title: Geometry Matters in Packed 3D Attention
papers.summary: Packing a 3D volume into a token sequence is not merely long-sequence modeling. Once the volume is packed, sequence order no longer encodes the geometry of the sample---so a positional mechanism indexed by sequence position can learn the memory layout rather than the object. This is a general failure mode for attention over packed geometric data. We introduce PACK3D, a local-global attention operator that separates memory layout from attention geometry. PACK3D keeps local neighborhood attention exact, compresses only distant context into contiguous 3D block summaries, and indexes every query-key interaction with axial RoPE on true token-grid coordinates rather than packed positions. Because the rotation is applied before a block is summarized, the query-to-summary logit remains a weighted sum of query-relative 3D displacements; compressed global context therefore stays spatially interpretable after packing, instead of collapsing to anonymous pooled content. We measure the failure mode directly. On a controlled synthetic task---train on one packing, change only the memory order of the tokens, hold the physical labeling rule fixed---learned positional embeddings and packed-sequence RoPE solve the training layout perfectly yet collapse under Morton, block-contiguous, and random repacking, while axial grid-coordinate RoPE stays exact throughout. The same coordinate system carries to real data: on Allen WTC-11 hiPSC microscopy, PACK3D improves over a parameter-matched 3D U-Net on the 15-structure joint task and over a matched learned-position local-global baseline, with controls isolating the coordinate system, not encoder capacity, as the source of the gain. A fused Triton implementation matches windowed-attention latency at 65k tokens while supplying the long-range context windowing cannot---so the operator is not only correct but trainable at scale.

papers.title: inkGround: Benchmarking Fine-grained Visual Grounding Capabilities of Vision-Language Models for Cursive Handwriting in the Wild
papers.summary: Human handwriting is produced as an ordered sequence of pen movements, but an offline image keeps only the final ink. Handwriting trajectory recovery aims to restore the ordered stroke points and their pen-up/pen-down transitions. Existing image-trajectory pair datasets are recorded with digitizing tablets under controlled conditions, which limits writer coverage and stylistic diversity. Moreover, there is no benchmark that measures the visual grounding capabilities of general-purpose Vision-Language Models (VLMs) for the stroke trajectory recovery task. In this work, we introduce inkGround, a benchmark for stroke trajectory recovery from full-page, camera-captured handwriting. inkGround pairs 537 page images (~18.7k words, ~163k strokes) with reference trajectories produced by a pretrained offline-to-online model, filtered by OCR agreement, and verified by human raters. Because these references are pseudo-labels that represent one plausible pen trajectory, we also evaluate VLMs on the IAM-OnDB dataset, which provides recorded pen trajectories. We cast the task as text-conditioned point grounding: given a page image and a target word, the model must locate the word and output its ordered stroke points. Outputs are scored by trajectory fidelity (DTW, Chamfer distance), readability of the rendered strokes (Accurate Rate, Correct Rate), and style similarity. We benchmark four open-source and three frontier closed-source VLMs with a shared in-context prompt. Closed-source models, notably Gemini-3.1-Pro, produce legible trajectories close to the reference, and this ranking also holds on IAM-OnDB.

papers.title: The Search for Statistical Indistinguishability Between Real and Fake Images
papers.summary: Images produced by generative models appear strikingly similar to real ones. In this work, we study whether perfection has been reached by generated content in terms of matching the properties of real data. We train deep neural networks to separate real data from fake and observe their test accuracies. Only a chance performance has any scope of proving statistical indistinguishability. However, since generative models are known to sometimes introduce small errors, e.g., low level checkerboard artifacts, we create progressive abstractions of the original real/fake images to potentially bring them to a space where those artifacts get wiped away. These include operations such as blurring, downsizing, cropping, converting RGB images into edge/semantic maps, etc. To our surprise, almost none of the abstractions are able to make fake data indistinguishable from real. The only cases when neural network based classifiers fail to separate the two categories is when the data is abstracted to such an extent that the original content seems mostly lost to the human eye, e.g., downsizing a $256 \times 256$ RGB image of human face to $4 \times 4$ resolution. We observe this trend across four different datasets of varying complexity (MNIST, CelebA, FFHQ and GenImage) and across various types of generative models (GANs, VAEs, diffusion models). This shows that the nature of fake artifacts extends all the way from low level to very high level in images. The simple implication is that fake images are much more different from real than we are used to think.
papers.title_zh: 真实图像与伪造图像之间统计不可区分性的探索
papers.abstract_zh: 生成模型产生的图像看起来与真实图像惊人地相似。在本工作中，我们研究生成内容在匹配真实数据属性方面是否已经达到完美。我们训练深度神经网络来区分真实数据与伪造数据，并观察其测试准确率。只有达到随机水平的表现，才可能证明统计不可区分性。然而，由于已知生成模型有时会引入小误差，例如低层棋盘格伪影，我们创建原始真实/伪造图像的渐进式抽象，以有可能将它们带入一个这些伪影被消除的空间。这些操作包括模糊、缩小、裁剪、将 RGB 图像转换为边缘/语义图等。令我们惊讶的是，几乎没有任何一种抽象能够使伪造数据与真实数据不可区分。基于神经网络的分类器唯一无法区分这两个类别的情况，是当数据被抽象到这样一种程度：原始内容在人眼看来似乎大部分已经丢失，例如将一张 $256 \times 256$ 的人脸 RGB 图像缩小到 $4 \times 4$ 分辨率。我们在四个复杂度不同的数据集（MNIST、CelebA、FFHQ 和 GenImage）上，以及在各种类型的生成模型（GAN、VAE、扩散模型）上，都观察到了这一趋势。这表明伪造伪影的本质在图像中从低层一直延伸到非常高的高层。其简单含义是，伪造图像与真实图像的差异远比我们通常认为的要大得多。

papers.title: CLaW: Codec-Guided Adaptive Latent Watermarking for Traceable Diffusion Image Generation
papers.summary: With the rapid advancement of text-to-image diffusion models, increasingly realistic AI-generated content has raised serious concerns about misuse and copyright infringement. Digital watermarking offers a promising solution by enabling user-level traceability, yet existing methods remain difficult to deploy at scale, hindered by costly model retraining or detection, poor effectiveness-fidelity trade-offs, and limited robustness to image transformations. To address these challenges, we propose CLaW (Codec-guided Latent Watermarking), a robust and efficient watermarking framework for traceable diffusion image generation with frozen diffusion backbones and inversion-free detection. Specifically, CLaW first uses a pretrained watermark codec to map each watermark message to a latent residual, enabling low-cost sampling-time injection. Then, the residual is injected within a late denoising window, where image semantics are better preserved and the watermark signal is less perturbed by subsequent denoising updates, yielding a better balance between watermark effectiveness and image fidelity. Furthermore, we introduce a decoder-guided adaptive injection mechanism that uses decoding confidence as feedback to dynamically calibrate watermark strength, reinforcing weak watermark signals and improving robustness under image transformations. Extensive experiments show that CLaW preserves high visual fidelity and achieves state-of-the-art robustness under image transformations, enabling reliable user-level traceability.
papers.title_zh: CLaW：用于可追溯扩散图像生成的编解码器引导自适应潜在水印
papers.abstract_zh: 随着文本到图像扩散模型的快速发展，日益逼真的 AI 生成内容引发了对其被滥用和版权侵权的严重担忧。数字水印通过实现用户级可追溯性提供了一种有前景的解决方案，然而现有方法仍难以大规模部署，受限于代价高昂的模型重训练或检测、效果与保真度之间不佳的权衡，以及对图像变换的鲁棒性有限。为应对这些挑战，我们提出 CLaW（Codec-guided Latent Watermarking，编解码器引导的潜在水印），一个面向可追溯扩散图像生成的鲁棒且高效的水印框架，其具有冻结的扩散骨干网络和无需反演的检测。具体而言，CLaW 首先使用预训练的水印编解码器将每条水印消息映射为潜在残差，从而实现低成本的采样时注入。然后，该残差在后期去噪窗口内被注入，此时图像语义得到更好的保留，且水印信号受后续去噪更新的扰动更小，从而在水印有效性与图像保真度之间取得更好的平衡。此外，我们引入一种解码器引导的自适应注入机制，该机制以解码置信度作为反馈来动态校准水印强度，增强微弱的水印信号并提高图像变换下的鲁棒性。大量实验表明，CLaW 保持了高视觉保真度，并在图像变换下实现了最先进的鲁棒性，从而能够实现可靠的用户级可追溯性。

papers.title: DeCoRL: Decomposed Consistency Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Image Composition
papers.summary: Multi-image composition (MICo) is a critical yet challenging capability for large-scale image editing models, where consistency degrades rapidly as the number of reference images increases. While supervised fine-tuning (SFT) can equip models with basic MICo ability, it provides only implicit supervision on the composed image and often fails to learn reliable object-level correspondence across multiple references. We propose DeCoRL, a reinforcement-learning (RL) framework that improves MICo consistency by decomposing holistic MICo consistency into object-level consistency. DeCoRL first establishes instruction-relevant object correspondences across reference images and localizes the corresponding regions in the generated image. It then uses a VLM-based reward model trained on single-object consistency annotations to produce fine-grained, object-wise feedback, which is aggregated into a multi-object consistency reward to guide RL post-training. We further introduce DeCo-Bench, a benchmark covering compositions from 2 to 6 reference images. Experiments on DeCo-Bench and the public MICo-Bench demonstrate consistent improvements in MICo consistency.

papers.title: WorldFlow: Joint Video and 3D Motion Prediction via Large-Scale Pretraining
papers.summary: Predicting future physical states stands as a central challenge in embodied intelligence. Existing video world models leave 3D dynamics implicit, action-based formulations remain tied to specific robot configurations, and 3D motion prediction models use flow-only supervision, providing a limited learning signal for physical dynamics. To circumvent these limitations, we introduce \method{}, a generative world model that jointly predicts future video and query-based 3D trajectories. By parameterizing 3D motion as continuous displacement tokens aligned with the video grid, a unified Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) backbone jointly denoises both modalities under a rectified-flow objective. This formulation couples explicit geometric dynamics with visual evolution, effectively unlocking the physical commonsense embedded within pretrained video models. To empirically scale and validate this unified architecture, we train \method{} on a heterogeneous mixture of 1.44 million object-level samples spanning simulated and real-world domains. We further introduce WorldFlowBench, comprising 1,678 evaluation samples from 11 data sources across simulated and real-world interactions, including spatial reasoning tasks. Across all three evaluation sets, WorldFlow achieves the lowest average displacement error (ADE) and final displacement error (FDE) among the evaluated learning-based methods. Notably, on the challenging SpatialCog set, WorldFlow achieves an ADE of 0.060 m, a 54.2\% reduction compared with the strongest external baseline. It also reduces ADE and FDE by 55.9\% and 68.5\%, respectively, compared with its flow-only variant. Project page: https://worldflow-rbs.github.io/.

papers.title: Unlocking Any-Order Generation in Pretrained Autoregressive Image Models
papers.summary: Autoregressive (AR) image generators are powerful in principle but inflexible in practice: training with a fixed raster-scan order hardcodes a single factorization of the image distribution into the model, leaving it unable to inpaint, outpaint, or edit at inference time. Existing solutions, including the modern discrete-diffusion family, train from scratch on a mixture of token orderings, paying roughly 3x the compute of standard raster-scan training; discrete diffusion further sacrifices compatibility with the AR inference ecosystem (KV caching, vLLM) by construction. We argue that this cost is unnecessary. A pretrained raster-scan AR model has already learned the joint distribution over image tokens; what it lacks is not knowledge but the ability to express that knowledge through non-sequential conditional pathways. We propose a recipe for adapting pretrained raster-scan models into any-order generators using two components: future-aware positional embeddings that resolve a target-position identifiability problem at negligible overhead, and an ordering curriculum that traces a stable optimization path from the pretrained solution to a good any-order basin. Applied to four base models across two architectures and two scales (LlamaGen-L/XL, RAR-L/XL), the recipe substantially outperforms MaskGIT on ImageNet inpainting (FID 6.21 vs. 10.44) and outpainting, is competitive with MAR-L, trades a 1.2-1.9 increase in class-conditional FID for this flexibility, and costs 13-33% additional compute beyond pretraining, while leaving the standard AR inference stack untouched. Inpainting, outpainting, and editing, our results suggest, need not be added to autoregressive image models. They can be unlocked from the ones that exist. Code is available at https://github.com/Ordered-AR/unlockedadaptation.
papers.title_zh: 解锁预训练自回归图像模型中的任意顺序生成
papers.abstract_zh: 自回归（AR）图像生成器在原理上很强大，但在实践中缺乏灵活性：使用固定的光栅扫描顺序进行训练会将图像分布的一种单一因子分解硬编码到模型中，使其在推理时无法进行图像修复、外扩或编辑。现有解决方案，包括现代离散扩散系列，在混合的 token 顺序上从头训练，所付出的计算量约为标准光栅扫描训练的 3 倍；离散扩散从构造上进一步牺牲了与 AR 推理生态（KV 缓存、vLLM）的兼容性。我们认为这种代价是不必要的。一个预训练的光栅扫描 AR 模型已经学习了图像 token 的联合分布；它所缺乏的不是知识，而是通过非序列的条件路径来表达该知识的能力。我们提出了一种将预训练光栅扫描模型适配为任意顺序生成器的方案，使用两个组件：未来感知的位置嵌入，以可忽略的开销解决目标位置可识别性问题；以及一种顺序课程，它追踪从预训练解到良好任意顺序盆地的稳定优化路径。应用于跨两种架构和两种规模的四个基础模型（LlamaGen-L/XL、RAR-L/XL）时，该方案在 ImageNet 图像修复（FID 6.21 对 10.44）和外扩上大幅优于 MaskGIT，与 MAR-L 具有竞争力，以类条件 FID 增加 1.2-1.9 换取这种灵活性，并且在预训练之外仅增加 13-33% 的计算量，同时保持标准 AR 推理栈不变。我们的结果表明，图像修复、外扩和编辑不必被添加到自回归图像模型中。它们可以从现有的模型中解锁。代码可在 https://github.com/Ordered-AR/unlockedadaptation 获取。

papers.title: Telling Is Not Seeing: Textual Personas Rarely Make Vision-Language Models Answer Like the People They Describe
papers.summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) are increasingly prompted with personas, such as "You have low vision", to stand in for people in user studies. We ask whether a persona makes a model see like the person it describes. We compare persona answers with measured people with low vision, color blindness or hearing loss, and with simple rules that use only the facts the persona states. The persona never beats these rules, and it erases the real differences between groups and individuals. Describing blur leaves recognition unchanged in all 14 models we test, while blurring the photo lowers it as it does for people. Inside open models, the description changes neither the image information nor the answer probabilities. Yet the models know the effects they fail to show: they can estimate how blur and illusions affect people. Telling is not seeing: a persona makes a model say what it knows about people, not see what they see.

papers.title: Semantic Mismapping in Generalized Category Discovery: Evaluation and Mitigation
papers.summary: Generalized Category Discovery (GCD) aims to perform old-category recognition and novel-category discovery in the same unlabeled set. Early methods address both objectives through clustering and evaluate the exchangeable predicted indices with global Hungarian (GH) matching. Recent methods adopt trainable parametric heads, using supervision for old-category recognition and discovery-oriented objectives for new categories. In this way, the output space becomes partially exchangeable: old indices are semantically anchored, while new indices remain exchangeable. However, these methods still apply global matching, which can reassign anchored old indices to other categories and hide some prediction errors. Empirically, we are surprised to observe that this reassignment can induce an overestimation of new-category accuracy by up to 25.63 points. We term this phenomenon semantic mismapping and further derive a permutation-cycle condition that characterizes when semantic mismapping can increase the global matching score. To fix this issue, we propose Semantics-Preserving Evaluation (SPE), which preserves the supervised semantics of old indices and restricts Hungarian matching to the new region. Furthermore, we propose Mismapping-Mitigating Optimization (MMO) to alleviate the prediction errors that can give rise to semantic mismapping, combining a region-balance loss (RBL) for old/new routing with a novel-diversity loss (NDL) that encourages orthogonality among new prototypes. Theoretically, we show that minimizing the two losses can tighten an upper bound on spurious accuracy gains from semantic mismapping, with controllable residual terms. Empirical results under both GH and SPE demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed method.

papers.title: SymKL: A Unified Representation-Space Measure of Signal Degradation
papers.summary: Quantifying degradation between a pristine signal and its degraded observation is fundamental to signal processing, yet existing full-reference measures are inherently modality-specific. We introduce SymKL, a unified full-reference degradation measure based on implicit neural representations (INRs). An INR is fitted once to the pristine reference and characterized by its diagonal Fisher information, which captures the local information geometry of the learned representation. Evaluating the Fisher information with the pristine reference and a degraded observation yields two parameter-sensitivity profiles whose symmetric KL divergence defines the degradation score. The proposed formulation requires only the reference and degraded observation, without knowledge of the corruption process or degradation severity, making it applicable across images, audio, and 3D data. We further derive an exact closed-form expression for the diagonal Fisher of SIREN, enabling efficient computation. Experiments on image, speech, and volumetric 3D benchmarks demonstrate that SymKL accurately tracks degradation severity, remains monotonic where conventional metrics saturate or fail, and provides a unified modality-agnostic measure of signal degradation. Code will be made publicly available after the review process.

papers.title: Diagnosing the Reference Gap: What Visual Scaffolds Can and Cannot Fix in Multimodal Reasoning
papers.summary: Multimodal large language models can recognize visual content yet struggle to reason reliably over it across multiple steps. In counting, a model may see all objects but lose track of which ones it has counted. We argue that such failures, commonly attributed to perception, reveal a reference gap: the failure to bind language to the relevant visual entities, regions, or locations. Motivated by the theory of visual routines, we test whether external references such as numbering can narrow this gap. We introduce ReGap-Bench, a paired benchmark of five visual reasoning tasks in which the scene, question, and answer are fixed and only the reference varies. Results show that task-matched references improve accuracy by up to 25\%, while mismatched references provide little benefit or even hurt performance. These findings identify the reference gap as a bottleneck distinct from visual perception and show that constructing task-appropriate visual references can serve as a training-free visual skill for improving multimodal reasoning.
papers.title_zh: 诊断参照鸿沟：视觉支架在多模态推理中能修复什么、不能修复什么
papers.abstract_zh: 多模态大语言模型能够识别视觉内容，却难以在多个步骤中对其可靠地进行推理。在计数任务中，模型可能看到了所有物体，却会失去对哪些物体已被计数的追踪。我们认为，这类通常被归因于感知的失败揭示出一种参照鸿沟：即未能将语言绑定到相关的视觉实体、区域或位置。受视觉程序理论的启发，我们检验了诸如编号之类的外部参照能否缩小这一鸿沟。我们提出了 ReGap-Bench，这是一个包含五项视觉推理任务的配对基准，其中场景、问题和答案均固定不变，只有参照发生变化。结果表明，与任务相匹配的参照可将准确率提升最多 25\%，而与任务不匹配的参照几乎不能带来收益，甚至会损害性能。这些发现将参照鸿沟识别为一种区别于视觉感知的瓶颈，并表明构建与任务相适配的视觉参照可以作为一种无需训练的视觉技能，用于改进多模态推理。

papers.title: FDSML: Formula-Driven Supervised Metric Learning with Parameter-Aware Triplet Loss
papers.summary: Formula-Driven Supervised Learning (FDSL) enables vision pre-training without real images, but existing methods cast pre-training as classification on discretized labels, discarding continuity in the generative process. We propose Formula-Driven Supervised Metric Learning (FDSML), which derives relational supervision from image-generation parameters beyond discrete class labels. FDSML combines FineFractalDB, our refined fractal dataset with higher intra-class variation and more stable structures, with a Parameter-Aware Triplet (PA-Triplet) Loss that assigns positives and negatives according to distances in the underlying Iterated Function System parameter space. This objective trains embeddings to respect parameter-derived relative similarity orderings. Experiments show that FDSML improves transferability to image retrieval while remaining competitive on downstream classification and improving robustness under several corruption settings. On ResNet-50, Recall@1 improves from 65.6% to 74.0% on Stanford Online Products and from 56.2% to 78.4% on Stanford Cars over FDSL pre-training. These results suggest that parameter-derived relational supervision provides a stronger synthetic pre-training signal than label-based classification for transfer beyond recognition.

papers.title: Agent-Wise Test-Time Normalization for Camera-Based Cooperative Perception with Corrupted Collaborators
papers.summary: Intermediate-fusion cooperative perception lets a vehicle detect objects beyond its own field of view by fusing features shared by nearby agents. When only a collaborator's cameras are degraded by fog, motion blur or exposure errors, the features it shares drift away from the training distribution while the ego input stays clean, and cooperation can become worse than not cooperating at all. Test-time batch-normalization adaptation, the standard training-free remedy, estimates statistics over the pooled batch of all agents and therefore normalizes both the clean ego and the corrupted collaborator with a mixture of two distributions. We show that this mixing harms even the clean ego: when the ego shares BN statistics with a corrupted collaborator, its detection from its own features drops by 3.58 to 6.68 AP@0.5 points although its cameras are untouched. We propose AgentNorm, an agent-wise test-time normalization that i) estimates the normalization statistics of every collaborator from its own current observation and ii) anchors the ego to its source statistics, so that the ego path remains exactly the original model. AgentNorm has no learnable parameters, needs no gradients or labels, is independent of the order of test frames, and runs locally on each agent without changing the transmitted features. On camera-based OPV2V with four fusion checkpoints and collaborator-only corruptions, AgentNorm raises AP@0.5 under severity-5 fog from 29.42-37.25 to 43.32-58.86 and outperforms pooled normalization by 5.53-12.94 points under fog and motion blur, at an extra latency of 2.3 ms per frame. On the real-world DAIR-V2X-C dataset, it outperforms pooled normalization in all ten infrastructure-corruption settings. We also report the cases it does not fix: occlusion, which removes image content rather than shifting feature statistics, and the case in which all agents share the same shift.

papers.title: ROAD: Modern Adversarial Training for Simple One-Step Distillation at Scale
papers.summary: One-step distillation turns pretrained diffusion models into fast generators, but strong results often require substantial training machinery and compute. Pure adversarial distillation offers a simpler route, yet has struggled at modern text-to-image scale. To address this limitation, we propose ROAD (Representation-grounded One-step Adversarial Distillation), a one-stage framework that distills text-to-image models with one adversarial objective and a lightweight representation-space critic. First, we replace the classical convolutional head with a Lipschitz-controlled Transformer head with token-level text conditioning, which matches the semantic tokens of modern visual encoders. Second, we observed a fixed random feature mixing leads to long-horizon degradation. We attribute it to generator-critic co-adaptation around one realization-specific view, and periodically re-draw the mixing to keep the randomization effective. Third, for our dense and vector-valued logits, we introduce Jacobian R1 which penalizes the full input-logit Jacobian, overcoming pooled R1's limitation of neglecting most of logit sensitivities. A single adversarial objective then suffices: in one step, ROAD reaches 11.03 FID on SDXL and 13.73 on SD3.5-M on COCO-10K, surpassing the multi-step teachers at a fraction of distribution matching's training compute.
papers.title_zh: ROAD：面向大规模简单一步蒸馏的现代对抗训练
papers.abstract_zh: 一步蒸馏将预训练扩散模型转变为快速生成器，但强结果往往需要大量训练机制和计算。纯对抗蒸馏提供了一条更简单的路径，但在现代文本到图像规模上一直难以奏效。为解决这一局限，我们提出 ROAD（Representation-grounded One-step Adversarial Distillation，基于表征的一步对抗蒸馏），这是一个单阶段框架，用一个对抗目标和一个轻量级表征空间判别器来蒸馏文本到图像模型。首先，我们用具有 token 级文本条件作用的 Lipschitz 受控 Transformer 头替换经典卷积头，其与现代视觉编码器的语义 token 相匹配。其次，我们观察到固定的随机特征混合会导致长时程退化。我们将其归因于生成器与判别器围绕某一个特定实现视图的协同适应，并周期性地重新抽取混合以保持随机化有效。第三，针对我们稠密且向量值的 logits，我们引入 Jacobian R1，它对完整的输入-logit Jacobian 施加惩罚，克服了池化 R1 忽略大部分 logit 敏感性的局限。随后单一对抗目标就足够了：在一步内，ROAD 在 COCO-10K 上于 SDXL 达到 11.03 FID，于 SD3.5-M 达到 13.73 FID，以分布匹配训练计算量的一小部分超越了多步教师模型。

papers.title: Comprehensive empirical evaluation of feature extractors in computer vision
papers.summary: Feature detection and matching are fundamental components in computer vision, underpinning a broad spectrum of applications. This study offers a comprehensive evaluation of traditional feature detections and descriptors, analyzing methods such as Scale Invariant Feature Transform (SIFT), Speeded-Up Robust Features (SURF), Binary Robust Independent Elementary Features (BRIEF), Oriented FAST and Rotated BRIEF (ORB), Binary Robust Invariant Scalable Keypoints (BRISK), KAZE, Accelerated KAZE (AKAZE), Fast Retina Keypoint (FREAK), Dense and Accurate Invariant Scalable descriptor for Yale (DAISY), Features from Accelerated Segment Test (FAST), and STAR. Each feature extractor was assessed based on its architectural design and complexity, focusing on how these factors influence computational efficiency and robustness under various transformations. Utilizing the Image Matching Challenge Photo Tourism 2020 dataset, which includes over 1.5 million images, the study identifies the FAST algorithm as the most efficient detector when paired with the ORB descriptor and Brute-Force (BF) matcher, offering the fastest feature extraction and matching process. ORB is notably effective on affine transformed and brightened images, while AKAZE excels in conditions involving blurring, fisheye distortion, image rotation, and perspective distortions. Through more than 2 million comparisons, the study highlights the feature extractors that demonstrate superior resilience across various conditions, including rotation, scaling, blurring, brightening, affine transformations, perspective distortions, fisheye distortion, and salt-and-pepper noise

papers.title: Evaluating Cultural Knowledge Editing in Vision-Language Models
papers.summary: Current Vision-Language Models (VLMs) frequently fail to recognize culture-specific concepts, especially from underrepresented regions. Effectively injecting this long-tail knowledge into existing models remains a challenge. In this work, we investigate knowledge editing as a targeted alternative by introducing CulturalBind, a benchmark comprising 3.2K images of 1K concepts from 6 domains, designed to evaluate culture-aware cross-modal knowledge as well as concept-level knowledge editing in VLMs. Pre-edit evaluation reveals that textual and visual knowledge is decoupled: models often demonstrate text-based knowledge of cultural concepts but fail to identify them from images. We then evaluate editing methods in single and sequential scenarios. Although current methods successfully correct individual visual recognition errors, they exhibit low cross-modal portability, failing to integrate edits into the model's broader parametric knowledge. Furthermore, performance degrades rapidly under sequential editing, highlighting the need for comprehensive adaptation approaches that better consolidate multimodal knowledge over time.

papers.title: Intrinsic Distribution Matching
papers.summary: One-step and few-step text-to-image generation must accurately render the details specified in the prompt despite limited opportunities for refinement. Distribution matching distillation (DMD) uses score differences to bring the generated distribution closer to a reference distribution. Following prior work, we estimate this difference with internal velocity branches, avoiding a separate fake-score network. We ask whether an explicit moment constraint improves this learned score supervision. A decomposition of the reverse-KL field into a Gaussian moment component and a non-Gaussian residual identifies statistics that can be constrained explicitly. We introduce Intrinsic Distribution Matching (IDM), which retains the full DMD correction and matches feature means and per-coordinate standard deviations using the generator's exponential-moving-average (EMA) copy, requiring no external feature encoder. Experiments use full-parameter and low-rank adaptation (LoRA) tuning on Z-Image-Turbo 6B and Qwen-Image 20B. At two network evaluations, IDM reaches 94.25% and 90.20% on Chinese and English LongText-Bench, the highest scores among the compared methods at this budget. Controlled ablations show gains from the added moment loss, while generator EMA features perform competitively with an external DINOv2 encoder across the five reported metrics. Code is available at https://github.com/inclusionAI/IDM.

papers.title: Where Do Vision Language Models Fail at 3D Reasoning?
papers.summary: Vision-language models can get individual judgments right while struggling to recover and consistently use the exact properties of a 3D object. To characterize this gap, we introduce BedBench, a controlled benchmark of thirteen procedurally generated tasks spanning individual judgments and composite answers. Across twelve open-weight and four frontier models, per-color counting exposes a pronounced weakness: humans achieve 93.3% accuracy, compared with 7.2% for the best model. Targeted fine-tuning raises one model's accuracy from 3.0% to 68.6%, but reveals a further difficulty: its answers about the most common colors remain inconsistent with its own per-color counts. Supplying those counts as text improves its judgments, showing that recovering a property does not mean using it consistently. Reasoning, scaling, and added visual cues each improve individual judgments, but none makes exact answers reliable. To locate the difficulty, we probe Qwen3.5-27B: exact per-color counts remain recoverable at the language model's input, yet the model's answers rarely recover them (65.0% for the probe vs. 3.0% for the model). Image-removal controls further show that some apparent successes require no visual evidence. These findings motivate evaluating 3D reasoning by exact correctness, consistent use, and image dependence, rather than accuracy alone. Code and dataset are publicly available: https://github.com/leduckhai/BedBench

papers.title: GROME: GROunding Factorized MEmory into Video World Models
papers.summary: Long-horizon consistency is essential for video world models, yet it becomes difficult to maintain once observed content falls outside the context window. Existing memory mechanisms either retrieve history as implicit context, which remains constrained by context capacity and entangles static and dynamic information or consolidate history into explicit global representations, which struggle to model evolving dynamics and accumulate geometric errors. To overcome these limitations, we introduce \textbf{GROME}, a novel factorized memory framework that augments video world models for long-horizon coherence across both static scenes and dynamic entities. GROME operates via three synergistic components: 1)~\emph{Static-Dynamic Factorization} decouples historical evidence into static and dynamic components, preserving static scene geometry and dynamic entity states separately; 2)~\emph{Local Memory Retrieval} selects spatially aligned static history to eliminate geometric drift alongside the latest dynamic entity states to ensure temporal continuity; 3)~\emph{Training-Free Memory Injection} seamlessly grounds the factorized memory into video world models via their native conditioning pathways. Experiments on long-horizon revisit scenarios demonstrate that GROME substantially enhances scene persistence and dynamic entity fidelity over existing methods, all while preserving the visual quality and controllability of the frozen backbone without additional training. Beyond self-rollouts, GROME readily accommodates external observations as plug-and-play memory, unlocking flexible and controllable video continuation and scene exploration.

papers.title: Aligning Medical Vision Language Models at the Capability Boundary with Entropy Adaptive Rubric Grounding
papers.summary: Medical diagnostic reasoning requires verifiable links between visual evidence and clinical knowledge, yet current medical vision language models are aligned with objectives that reward the wrong behavior. Uniform supervised fine tuning lets easy cases dominate updates while clinically critical boundary cases saturate prematurely. Sparse rewards based only on final-answer correctness cannot assess anatomical grounding or clinical logic, inviting reward hacking through answer shortcuts. We propose MedCBR, a two-stage alignment framework coupling boundary-aware preference optimization with rubric-grounded reinforcement learning. First, we construct counterfactual boundary preferences at the model's capability frontier using empirical pass rates and preference pairs that share reasoning prefixes but diverge at decisive diagnostic branches. Difficulty Weighted Boundary Preference Optimization (DBPO) concentrates learning on this calibrated boundary region. Second, we distill reusable clinical rubrics from boundary trajectories and activate them according to prediction entropy. Entropy Gated Grounded Policy Optimization (EGPO) rewards answer correctness, anatomical grounding, and reasoning fidelity while suppressing rubric noise on reliable samples. A reference policy anchored to the boundary-aligned model couples population-level boundary priors with instance-level uncertainty, making diagnostic reasoning more accurate and clinically grounded. Experiments on six medical benchmarks show consistent improvements over strong general, specialized, and reinforcement learning baselines, reaching 61.2% average accuracy with the largest gains on challenging differential diagnosis tasks. Ablations show super-additive gains: combining the two stages exceeds the sum of their individual improvements.

papers.title: LiDAR-SHIELD: A Fully Dockerized Adversarial Robustness Assessment Framework for LiDAR-Based 3D Perception Models
papers.summary: LiDAR-based 3D perception underpins autonomous driving and robotics, yet deploying these models safely requires stress-testing them against adversarial inputs before real-world use. Although state-of-the-art adversarial attacks exist, their implementations are often fragmented across individual repositories, each tied to a specific architecture or task and requiring manual environment reconstruction and model-specific integration code. We present LIDARSHIELD, a unified and fully Dockerized framework that reverses this workflow: rather than installing the target model inside the toolkit, LIDARSHIELD exposes any model through three lightweight HTTP endpoints, namely /info, /forward, and /gradient As a result, connecting a new model or dataset requires only a single loader function or adapter. The framework supports both 3D semantic segmentation and 3D object detection through the same engine-service protocol, integrating a task-aware suite of state-of-the-art attacks, including PGD and Square Attack for segmentation, and point perturbation, point removal, point injection, and LiDAttack for detection. This enables systematic exposure of corner cases and vulnerabilities across heterogeneous LiDAR backbones. The LiDAR-Shield codebase is publicly available at https://github.com/alexandrosgk/LiDAR-shield.

papers.title: sDMD: Sinkhorn Distribution Matching Distillation
papers.summary: Distribution Matching Distillation (DMD) distills multi-step diffusion models into few-step generators by minimizing reverse KL divergence. Despite its strong performance, DMD guides samples by local density alone, which introduces two limitations: teacher scores can be unreliable in regions of low teacher density, and the mode-seeking behavior of reverse KL can collapse the student onto a subset of the teacher modes. We first connect DMD to Wasserstein gradient flow, showing that its gradient follows from a fixed-point formulation with integral KL (IKL) as the energy functional. This perspective motivates augmenting IKL with an optimal transport term that addresses these limitations by guiding outlier samples toward the target and promoting mode coverage. We realize this term using Sinkhorn divergence estimated from finite batches. In practice, however, errors in the estimated Sinkhorn velocity can perturb in-domain samples for which IKL guidance is already accurate. To this end, we introduce sDMD, which adaptively activates the Sinkhorn correction based on discriminator outputs, focusing on outlier samples where IKL may be unreliable. With 2--4 sampling steps on FLUX.1-dev, Qwen-Image-20B, and Wan2.1-14B, sDMD outperforms distillation baselines on GenEval, DPG, WISE, and VBench while improving sample diversity over DMD2.
papers.title_zh: sDMD：Sinkhorn 分布匹配蒸馏
papers.abstract_zh: 分布匹配蒸馏（DMD）通过最小化反向 KL 散度，将多步扩散模型蒸馏为少步生成器。尽管其性能强劲，DMD 仅通过局部密度来引导样本，这带来了两个局限：在教师密度较低的区域，教师分数可能不可靠；反向 KL 的模式寻求行为可能使学生坍缩到教师模式的一个子集。我们首先将 DMD 与 Wasserstein 梯度流联系起来，表明其梯度来自以积分 KL（IKL）作为能量泛函的不动点表述。这一视角促使我们用一个最优传输项来增强 IKL，该项通过将离群样本引导向目标并促进模式覆盖来解决这些局限。我们使用从有限批次估计的 Sinkhorn 散度来实现该项。然而在实践中，估计得到的 Sinkhorn 速度中的误差可能会扰动域内样本，而对于这些样本，IKL 引导已经准确。为此，我们引入 sDMD，它基于判别器输出自适应地激活 Sinkhorn 校正，重点关注 IKL 可能不可靠的离群样本。在 FLUX.1-dev、Qwen-Image-20B 和 Wan2.1-14B 上以 2--4 个采样步数，sDMD 在 GenEval、DPG、WISE 和 VBench 上优于蒸馏基线，同时相比 DMD2 提升了样本多样性。

papers.title: Spectral Invariant Fusion and Refinement for Domain Generalized Semantic Segmentation
papers.summary: Domain generalized semantic segmentation is challenging because it requires accurate dense prediction on unseen domains without any access to target-domain data during training. Existing methods improve transferability through data diversification, invariant learning, or direct use of foundation models, but they often struggle to simultaneously suppress domain-sensitive interference and preserve fine-grained spatial cues. In this work, we propose SIFR, a frequency-aware dual-stream framework that tackles domain shift at both the fusion and decoding stages. SIFR uses spectral modeling as a unified principle to regulate both heterogeneous prior interaction and dense decoder refinement. Instead of directly fusing frozen CLIP and DINOv2 features, SIFR performs spectral-guided invariant fusion to filter out domain-sensitive responses while preserving complementary semantic and structural information. In addition, SIFR incorporates a spectral decoder refinement module that stabilizes multi-scale decoder features through low-frequency statistics-based normalization and adaptive frequency selection, thereby reducing the propagation of residual domain bias in dense prediction. This design enables SIFR to jointly improve domain robustness and segmentation precision under severe distribution shifts. Extensive experiments on multiple DGSS benchmarks, including synthetic-to-real, real-to-real, and adverse-weather settings, demonstrate consistent improvements over previous state-of-the-art methods.

papers.title: Mind The Gap (MTG-AD): Dataset and Fine-grained Evaluation for End-to-End Inline Audio Descriptions
papers.summary: Audio descriptions (AD) are essential for making visual media accessible to blind and low-vision (BLV) users. While Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) offer a scalable solution for generating audio descriptions on-demand, their performance on ``inline'' audio descriptions -- which must fit within existing silences in a video -- remains under-explored, particularly for diverse user-generated content (UGC). We present a comprehensive investigation into MLLM-generated inline audio descriptions. First, we introduce MTG-AD, a professionally annotated dataset of 36 hours of videos, each averaging $\sim$5 mins. and 8k+ descriptions in total, co-created by paired blind and sighted AD professionals to provide a high-quality benchmark for this task. Second, we propose MTG-AD-Eval, an evaluation framework based on audio description expert guidelines that provides fine-grained, reference-free actionable metrics for model improvement. Crucially, our framework evaluates the end-to-end task: it renders the generated scripts into audio tracks to assess their fit within the original video's natural silences, minimizing disruptive overlaps. Our analysis across frontier MLLMs reveals that while models accurately describe visual events and substantially reduce speech overlaps, gaps persist in narrative pacing and flow. Finally, we empirically validate that our automated and reference-free metrics correlate significantly with human quality ratings from sighted raters and 7 BLV participants, finding that while users narrowly prefer human-authored audio descriptions, they find MLLM-generated audio descriptions highly beneficial for comprehension. We provide actionable system design guidance and release MTG-AD at https://hf.co/datasets/google/mind-the-gap-inline-ad and MTG-AD-Eval at https://github.com/google/mtg-ad.
papers.title_zh: 关注差距（MTG-AD）：面向端到端内联音频描述的数据集与细粒度评估
papers.abstract_zh: 音频描述（AD）对于使视觉媒体能够被盲人和低视力（BLV）用户访问至关重要。尽管多模态大语言模型（MLLMs）为按需生成音频描述提供了一种可扩展的解决方案，但它们在“内联”音频描述——这类描述必须适配视频中已有的静音片段——上的表现仍未得到充分探索，尤其是在多样化的用户生成内容（UGC）上。我们对MLLM生成的内联音频描述进行了全面研究。首先，我们介绍MTG-AD，这是一个经过专业标注的数据集，包含36小时视频，每个视频平均时长$\sim$5分钟，总共有8k+条描述，由成对的盲人和视力正常AD专业人员共同创建，为该任务提供高质量基准。其次，我们提出MTG-AD-Eval，这是一个基于音频描述专家指南的评估框架，为模型改进提供细粒度、无参考且可操作的指标。关键在于，我们的框架评估端到端任务：它将生成的脚本渲染为音频轨道，以评估其与原始视频自然静音片段的契合程度，并尽量减少破坏性重叠。我们对前沿MLLM的分析表明，尽管模型能够准确描述视觉事件并大幅减少语音重叠，但在叙事节奏和流畅性方面仍存在差距。最后，我们通过实验验证，我们的自动化且无参考的指标与视力正常评分者以及7名BLV参与者给出的人工质量评分显著相关；我们发现，尽管用户仅以微弱优势更偏好人工撰写的音频描述，但他们认为MLLM生成的音频描述对理解非常有帮助。我们提供可操作的系统设计指导，并在 https://hf.co/datasets/google/mind-the-gap-inline-ad 发布MTG-AD，在 https://github.com/google/mtg-ad 发布MTG-AD-Eval。

papers.title: EPC-RawDC: Equivariant Physics Constrained 3D Diffusion with Raw Data Consistency for CBCT to CT Image Synthesis
papers.summary: Cone beam computed tomography (CBCT) is widely used for image guided and adaptive radiotherapy, but scatter, noise, reconstruction artifacts, and inaccurate Hounsfield units limit its quantitative use. Recent diffusion approaches for CBCT to CT synthesis remain largely image driven, with limited use of the underlying acquisition physics. We propose EPC-RawDC, a conditional 3D latent diffusion framework that combines volumetric generative modeling with two complementary constraints derived from the same scanner specific CBCT forward model. First, geometry equivariant projection constraint exploits the rotational equivariance of the CBCT forward operator by supervising the synthesized CT through correspondingly transformed reference projections. Second, raw data consistency uses noisy projection measurements of the individual acquisition as scan specific supervision during training. The framework was evaluated on two independent clinical cohorts with distinct scanner geometries and projection sources. For JUST, the physics constraints used measured clinical raw CBCT projections acquired with an Elekta system, whereas for SynthRAD2025 the projection data were simulated from the reference CT using a Varian geometry with Poisson photon statistics. EPC-RawDC achieved an SSIM of 0.97 in both cohorts and improved PSNR over DDPM by 2.66 dB on SynthRAD2025 and 2.10 dB on JUST, while reducing mean MAE by 20.3% and 19.0%, respectively. On SynthRAD2025, projection consistency and equivariant errors were reduced by 55.0% and 41.4% relative to DDPM. These results demonstrate that combining a volumetric diffusion prior with scanner geometry and scan specific projection measurements improves quantitative CBCT to CT synthesis across both simulated and measured projection domains. Code available after publication at https://github.com/ALZAHRAALTALIB/EPC-RawDC.
papers.title_zh: EPC-RawDC：用于 CBCT 到 CT 图像合成的具有原始数据一致性的等变物理约束三维扩散
papers.abstract_zh: 锥形束计算机断层扫描（CBCT）广泛用于图像引导与自适应放疗，但散射、噪声、重建伪影以及不准确的 Hounsfield 单位限制了其定量应用。近期用于 CBCT 到 CT 合成的扩散方法在很大程度上仍然是图像驱动的，对底层采集物理的利用有限。我们提出 EPC-RawDC，一种条件三维潜在扩散框架，它将体数据生成建模与源自同一扫描仪特定 CBCT 前向模型的两个互补约束相结合。第一，几何等变投影约束通过经相应变换的参考投影对合成 CT 进行监督，从而利用 CBCT 前向算子的旋转等变性。第二，原始数据一致性在训练期间使用个体采集的含噪投影测量作为扫描特定监督。该框架在两个独立的临床队列上进行了评估，这些队列具有不同的扫描仪几何结构和投影来源。对于 JUST，物理约束使用的是由 Elekta 系统采集的实测临床原始 CBCT 投影，而对于 SynthRAD2025，投影数据则是使用具有泊松光子统计的 Varian 几何结构从参考 CT 模拟得到的。EPC-RawDC 在两个队列中均达到了 0.97 的 SSIM，并在 SynthRAD2025 上将 PSNR 较 DDPM 提高了 2.66 dB，在 JUST 上提高了 2.10 dB，同时分别将平均 MAE 降低了 20.3% 和 19.0%。在 SynthRAD2025 上，相对于 DDPM，投影一致性和等变误差分别降低了 55.0% 和 41.4%。这些结果表明，将体数据扩散先验与扫描仪几何结构以及扫描特定投影测量相结合，可在模拟和实测投影域中改善定量 CBCT 到 CT 合成。代码将在发表后发布于 https://github.com/ALZAHRAALTALIB/EPC-RawDC。

papers.title: Localizing Concepts in Visual Autoregressive Models
papers.summary: Understanding the internal routing of visual concepts is crucial for the safe and controllable adaptation of generative models. While concept localization has been widely studied in diffusion models, the emerging paradigm of next-scale visual autoregressive models remains largely unexplored.
